# Getting your coding agent running

<!-- GENERATED by logistics/scripts/stage_section_pages.py from sections/sec01/agent_setup.md. Do not edit here; edit the section file. -->

Budget fifteen minutes and finish with the acceptance test in §3. Your Harvard Claude account
already exists, so most of that time goes on the download.

This guide is written for **Claude Code**, which is the course default: §1 is the desktop app
and §2 is the same tool in a terminal. Do one of them. If you would rather use OpenAI's
tooling, the appendix covers ChatGPT and Codex, and either of those is fine for the course.

---

## 0. Your Harvard Claude account

Harvard provisions Claude through HarvardKey and you already have it. Sign in:

1. Go to <https://claude.ai/>
2. Enter your Harvard email address.
3. Click **Sign in with SSO**, which appears once the email is in the box.

If you already had a Claude account on your Harvard email, you may land in your old personal
workspace. Switch with the selector under your profile icon, top left.

HUIT's own write-up is [Getting Started with
Claude](https://harvard.service-now.com/ithelp?id=kb_article&sys_id=5a7a592c93e1c3503f737c7d1dba10bb).
If sign-in fails, post on Ed before filing an IT ticket. We can usually answer faster, and
whatever stopped you has probably stopped someone else.

> Use your Harvard account. Personal free tiers do not include agent access, and we cannot
> debug a subscription we cannot see.

---

## 1. Claude Code desktop app — the default

No terminal required.

1. Download from <https://claude.com/download> and install it. macOS and Windows have direct
   installers; on Linux see <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-linux>.
2. Open the app and sign in with the Harvard account from §0.
3. Point it at a folder. Make an empty one first — `am215/` somewhere you can find again — and
   open that. An agent works inside a folder, and it can read and write the files there.

Then run the acceptance test in §3.

---

## 2. Claude Code in the terminal

The same tool and the same account, driven from a shell. Pick this or §1, whichever you
prefer.

**macOS, Linux, or WSL:**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows PowerShell:**

```powershell
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then check it landed, make a working folder, and start it:

```bash
claude --version
```

```bash
mkdir -p ~/am215 && cd ~/am215 && claude
```

The first run opens a browser to sign in. If something is wrong and the error does not say
what, `claude doctor` prints a diagnostic without starting a session.

---

## 3. The two-minute acceptance test

Run this before you decide you are set up. In your working folder, give the agent exactly
this:

> Create a file called `check.py` that prints the numbers 1 to 10 and their squares. Then run
> it and show me the output.

You are ready when all three of these are true:

1. A file called `check.py` is in your folder when you go and look for it on disk.
2. The agent ran it and reported the output it got back.
3. You can find the folder again without the agent's help.

Code on screen with no file on disk means you have a chat interface. Try §1 once more; if that
fails too, §4 describes what the chat interface costs you.

---

## 4. If your laptop will not cooperate

Try §1 and §2 both before giving up on the machine; the desktop app and the CLI fail for
different reasons.

If neither runs, the web chat interfaces — claude.ai and chatgpt.com in a browser — will do.
They cannot create files, run code, or see errors, so you will be copying output back and
forth by hand. Say so on Ed, because a laptop that will not run either one is worth us
knowing about.

There is also a browser-based option that needs nothing installed, described in §A4. It puts
the agent inside VS Code or a Jupyter terminal, so it suits you better if you already know one
of those.

---

## 5. When it goes wrong

| What you see | What it usually is |
|---|---|
| Access error signing in at claude.ai | You already have access, so this is unexpected. Post on Ed. |
| No **Sign in with SSO** button | It appears only after you type your Harvard email. |
| Signed in, but everything looks like your old account | You are in a personal workspace. Switch under your profile icon. |
| `claude: command not found` after installing | Close the terminal and open a new one. If it persists, run `claude doctor`. |
| Windows: `'irm' is not recognized` | That command is PowerShell-only. PowerShell's prompt starts `PS C:\`. |
| Signed in, but it will not write files | The web chat has no file access. See §4. |
| Never used a terminal before | Use the desktop app (§1). Nothing in this course requires a terminal. |

**Still stuck when section starts?** Tell your TF in the first five minutes. You will pair
with someone in your group whose agent runs, and you do the typing.

**Stuck the night before?** Post on Ed. Setup problems repeat, so one answer usually helps
several people at once.

## Appendix — ChatGPT and Codex

Skip this unless you would rather work in OpenAI's tooling. Either tool below is acceptable
for the course, and neither is better supported than Claude Code.

### A1. Your Harvard ChatGPT account

HUIT pulled the course roster on **2 September** and emailed an invitation to every student
enrolled at that point. Harvard's ChatGPT licences are not wired to Grouper, so a student who
joined the roster afterwards does not get one automatically and adding them to the roster now
will not trigger it. Request an account here:
<https://harvard.service-now.com/ithelp?id=sc_cat_item&sys_id=53b1914133a083d074dca3813d5c7b2d>

Codex signs in with the same ChatGPT account.

### A2. ChatGPT desktop app

1. Download from <https://chatgpt.com/download> and install it.
2. Sign in with the Harvard ChatGPT account from §A1.
3. Make an empty working folder — `am215/`, somewhere you can find again.

Run the acceptance test in §3 before you rely on this one. The features that create and run
files sit behind a specific mode, and the app also has a plain chat window with no access to
your disk. §3 tells you which of the two you are in.

### A3. Codex in the terminal

**macOS or Linux:**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh
```

**Windows PowerShell:**

```powershell
irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex
```

If you already have Node 18 or later, `npm install -g @openai/codex` works too. Start it by
running `codex` inside your working folder and choosing **Sign in with ChatGPT**. Then run the
acceptance test in §3.

### A4. HUIT Open OnDemand — the agent in a browser

Open OnDemand runs a session in your browser with nothing installed on your machine. Claude
Code and Codex are both preinstalled there; you sign in with your own Harvard account as
usual.

You reach the agent through one of two apps. **Code Server** is VS Code in a browser tab, and
you drive the agent from a terminal panel inside it. **Jupyter Lab** gives you the same
environment with a Jupyter terminal instead. Either works, and both put a layer of editor
between you and the agent, so this is a better fit if you already use one of them.

The link and the current status are in the Ed announcement. Two things to know before you
rely on it: the sessions mount your real home directory and run with editor workspace trust
turned off, so keep anything sensitive out of them; and you choose a number of hours at launch,
after which the session ends.
